source.title: What drives LLM bail? A small Mech Interp study

record.file_problem: The supplied text refers to a plot/table, but their values are not included.
record.tranche_reason: It tests refusal-direction steering with a conditional mean-difference vector, but uses a different direction construction and intervention from the original all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.gate_note: Experiment 1 reports a qualitative double dissociation: the orthogonalized refusal vector steers refusal, while the bail SAE feature strongly steers bail and barely affects refusal. Experiment 2 reports bail-rate changes from explanation-prompt variations. These bail findings are recorded as related but outside the listed claim versions. The attention analysis concerns where the model attends, not refusal-direction effects; its reported null is not a row for a version. Details used to construct the directions or select the feature are not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study builds a difference-in-means refusal direction (refuse minus comply on harmful prompts, layer 31, Gemma-3-12B) and steers with it. It reports that this steers refusal rate, which bears on V1's causal-addition claim. The direction construction, the single layer and the steering differ from the original, and no numbers are given.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The author concludes that bail and refusal are mechanistically distinct, that bail is driven by explanation rather than discomfort, and that this argues against a welfare interpretation in these specific settings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses conditional mean-difference directions and activation steering, but constructs the refusal direction from refuse-versus-comply cases within the continue subset, de-mixes it using an SAE bail feature, and does not perform the original all-layer, all-position projection ablation. The study is a LessWrong post describing a small mechanistic study.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes with the intermission prompt: forbidding explanation reduces bail and requiring explanation increases it. The reported direction effects are at layer 31; no cross-layer comparison is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE feature 4957 strongly steers bail while barely affecting refusal. The orthogonalized refusal vector barely affects bail. The preliminary mean-difference directions were mixed across the two behaviours.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Gemma-3-12B's intermission setting, bail and refusal are steerable by distinct directions or features.

fits_no_version.finding: Forbidding explanation halves the bail rate; requiring explanation more than doubles it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explanation prompting causally increases bail in the intermission setting.

record.problems: The numeric results for the steering and prompt-ablation experiments are not present in the supplied text, which refers to a plot/table. The mechanistic results are limited to Gemma-3-12B and one bail mechanism. No general-capability check is reported. The reasoning-model evidence is qualitative, and the authors note possible evaluation awareness in Kimi K2-Thinking's reasoning traces.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible outcome rows omitted. The attention experiment is not included as a claim-version row because it measures attention patterns rather than refusal-direction effects.

untested.parts: Harmful-minus-harmless construction; directional ablation removing refusal across all layers and positions; inducing refusal on harmless prompts; preservation of other capabilities.
No jailbreak analysis or adversarial training.
No test of multi-direction or cone structure of refusal; the bail/refusal de-mixing concerns bail, not refusal geometry.
Harmfulness judgment is not measured separately from refusal.
No transfer across languages, model variants or base-to-instruct models.
No comparison of training methods or timing.
Kimi K2-Thinking is used only for qualitative chain-of-thought reading; no direction is tested in it.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong MATS application post; all steering results are figure-only with no numbers in the text. The bearing on V1 is weak: it is a single-layer additive steering result with a conditional refuse-vs-comply direction. There is no ablation and no capability check.

versions.untested_parts: The study steers a conditional refusal-versus-comply mean-difference direction, not the original harmful-minus-harmless direction. It does not report projecting the direction out at every layer and position, testing removal of refusals, adding it to harmless requests, or measuring preservation of general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is tested.
The bail/refusal double dissociation does not test whether refusal itself is affine, cone-shaped, or carried by multiple directions.
The study does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is tested.
Kimi K2-Thinking is used for qualitative bail-reasoning analysis, not for a refusal-direction intervention or test of V1.

labels.condition: Gemma-3-12B, layer 31, BailBench harmful prompts, steering-strength sweep during turn-1 generation
labels.reason: The text states that the orthogonalized refusal vector steers refusal independently of bail (r1). It tests only addition, with a refuse-minus-comply contrast on harmful prompts, and gives no numbers. Ablation and capabilities are untested.

relation.reason: The study reports its own result that adding a refusal mean-diff direction steers refusal rate, though only in words.

tranche.reason: The study asks whether bail and refusal are distinct, not whether a direction mediates refusal. Refusal steering is one arm of a dissociation in a new two-turn bail setting. Its method is close to the original (mean-diff plus addition, Arditi-style string match), but the contrast is refuse-minus-comply on harmful prompts. The result on refusal is qualitative only.

source_check.notes: The dissociation and prompt-ablation plots are not in the text, so Exp 1-2 give no rates, alpha values or steering n (only Exp 4 states alpha of -8000/0/+8000 with 50 samples). Bail steering acts only at turn 2, after turn 1 is sampled, so 'feature barely affects refusal' holds by design. The pack lists the V1 verdict without an [lN] id. This is an informal LessWrong/MATS-application post with no code.
